paper.title: Contextual Combinatorial Bandits with Changing Action Sets via Gaussian Processes

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual combinatorial multi-armed bandit with changing action sets (C3-MAB) with GP-sampled base arm outcomes
unmapped: Base arm expected outcome function f over context space is a sample from a Gaussian process with known kernel k(x,x)<=1
Expected super-arm reward u is a known monotone function, B-Lipschitz (in l1) in expected base-arm outcomes
Learner uses an alpha-approximation (deterministic) oracle; regret is alpha-approximation regret
Number of available base arms per round bounded by M (known, used in beta_t); super arm size at most K
Sequence of available context sets is arbitrary (regret holds for any given availability sequence)
settings.definition_quote: We assume that there exists a function $f:\XX \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$, such that we have $r(x)=f(x) +\eta$ ... $\eta \sim {\cal N} (0,\sigma^2)$ ... we model $f$ as a sample from a Gaussian process ... $R_{\alpha} (T)  =  \alpha \sum^T_{t=1}   \textup{opt}(f_t ) -  \sum^T_{t=1} u(f(  \bs{x}_{t,S_t}  ))$

algorithms.name: O'CLOK-UCB
requires_knowledge_of: M (max number of available base arms)

symbols.m: maximum cardinality K of any feasible super arm (paper's K)
symbols.B_lip: Lipschitz constant B of expected reward w.r.t. expected base arm outcomes
symbols.lambda_star: maximum eigenvalue of posterior covariance matrices of selected actions over T rounds (lambda^*(K))
symbols.M_max: upper bound M on number of available base arms per round
symbols.gamma_KT: maximum information gain over feasible super-arm context sequences given the available context sets X_1..X_T

conditions: f sampled from GP with k(x,x)<=1

source.label: mainthm
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1)$, $T \in \mathbb{N}$. Given $\beta_t = 2\log (M\pi^2t^2/ 3\delta )$, the regret incurred by O'CLOK-UCB in $T$ rounds is upper bounded as $R_{\alpha}(T) \leq \sqrt{C(K)K\beta_T T \gamma_{KT}(\mathcal{X}_{\overline{T}})},$ with probability at least $1-\delta$,  where $C(K)= 8B^2(\lambda^*(K)+\sigma^2)$, and $\lambda^*(K)$ is the maximum eigenvalue of all covariance matrices of selected actions over $T$ rounds.

results.notes: Alpha-approximation regret; probability over GP sample and noise. lambda_star is a data-dependent quantity. beta_t schedule does not depend on T, so anytime.
